messages.subject: Re: Error in custom distribution - Dimension of distribution argument(s) does not match required dimension(s)
parts:
Heather, in your model code, the usage of dRWTrajectoryPotential (directly below)

      s[i,1:2,t] ~ dRWTrajectoryPotential(kappa=k[age[i,t-1]+1], s.pre = s[i,1:2,t-1], pix.pre = pix[i,t-1],
                                        omega = omega[age[i,t-1]+1],
                                        east = east[pix[i,t-1],t], north = north[pix[i,t-1],t],
                                        xmin=xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax)

The following arguments are passed *scalar* values:

kappa=k[age[i,t-1]+1]
pix.pre = pix[i,t-1]
omega[age[i,t-1]+1]
east = east[pix[i,t-1],t]
north = north[pix[i,t-1],t]

Your distribution is expecting (requires) *vector* values for these, which would be something more like:

kappa=k[(age[i,t-1]+1) : N]
pix.pre = pix[i, 1:T]
omega = omega[age[i,t-1] : 5]
east = east[pix[i,t-1], 2:t]
north = north[pix[i,t-1], 1:T]

I'm not saying those are correct at all, I just modified them to be *vectors*.  Note how each one contains something of the form N:M, which specifies a *vector* range from the indexed arrays, which is more than just a single (scalar) element.  Does this make sense?  If not, I suspect the Nimble User Manual has more examples of this.

Keep at it,
Daniel





On Fri, Jun 9, 2023 at 1:49 PM heather...@gmail.com <heather...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello,

I'm trying to write a custom function to deal with a correlated random walk in a bounded state space. However, I must be specifying the dimensions of my problem incorrectly, as the function gives me the error:

Error in model$checkBasics() :
  Dimension of distribution argument(s) 'kappa,pix.pre,omega,east,north' does not match required dimension(s) for the distribution 'dRWTrajectoryPotential'. Necessary dimension(s) are 1,1,1,1,1. You may need to ensure that you have explicit vectors and not one-row or one-column matrices.

Here is the distribution and random generator I've written:
deregisterDistributions("dRWTrajectoryPotential")
dRWTrajectoryPotential <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1), kappa=double(1), s.pre = double(1), pix.pre = double(1),
                 omega = double(1), 
                 east = double(1), north = double(1),
                 xmin=double(0), xmax = double(0), ymin = double(0), ymax = double(0),
                 log = integer(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double(0))
   
    loglike<-rep(0, 2)
    mu<-rep(0, 2)
   
    # locations for occasions >1
 
    mu[1]<- (s.pre[1] +  east*omega) #*(1-a) + s.parent[1]*a           #gradient in X
    mu[2]<- (s.pre[2] + north*omega) #*(1-a)+ s.parent[2]*a        #gradient in Y
   
    # truncated normal
    loglike[1] <- dnorm(x[1], mu[1], sd=sqrt(1/kappa), log=TRUE)- log((pnorm(xmax, mu[1], sd=sqrt(1/kappa)) - pnorm(xmin, mu[1], sd=sqrt(1/kappa))))
    loglike[2] <- dnorm(x[2], mu[2], sd=sqrt(1/kappa), log=TRUE)- log((pnorm(ymax, mu[2], sd=sqrt(1/kappa)) - pnorm(ymin, mu[2], sd=sqrt(1/kappa))))
   
    ans <- sum(loglike[1:2])
    if(log) return(ans)
    else return(exp(ans))
   
  }
)

#random value generator
rRWTrajectoryPotential  <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(n = integer(0), kappa=double(1), s.pre = double(1), pix.pre = double(1),
                 omega = double(1),
                 east = double(1), north = double(1),
                 xmin=double(0), xmax = double(0), ymin = double(0), ymax = double(0)) {
    returnType(double(1))
   
    x<-rep(0, 2)
    mu<-rep(0, 2)
   
    mu[1]<- s.pre[1] +  (east[1]*omega[1]) #*(1-a) + s.parent[1]*a           #gradient in X
    mu[2]<- s.pre[2] + (north[1]*omega[1]) #*(1-a)+ s.parent[2]*a        #gradient in Y
   
    # nimble functions don't seem to like rtnorm. Write out truncated normal instead.
    tmp.x <- runif(1, pnorm(xmin, mu[1], sd=sqrt(1/kappa[1])), pnorm(xmax, mu[1], sd=sqrt(1/kappa[1])))
    x[1] <- qnorm(tmp.x,  mu[1], sqrt(1/kappa[1]))
   
    tmp.y <- runif(1, pnorm(ymin, mu[2], sd=sqrt(1/kappa[1])), pnorm(ymax,  mu[2], sd=sqrt(1/kappa[1])))
    x[2] <- qnorm(tmp.y, mu[2], sqrt(1/kappa[1]))
   
    return(x[1:2])
  })

And here is how it's used in the code:
for(t in 2:nocc){
    for(i in 1:M){     
      s[i,1:2,t] ~ dRWTrajectoryPotential(kappa=k[age[i,t-1]+1], s.pre = s[i,1:2,t-1], pix.pre = pix[i,t-1],
                                        omega = omega[age[i,t-1]+1],
                                        east = east[pix[i,t-1],t], north = north[pix[i,t-1],t],
                                        xmin=xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax)


I think somehow the dimensions of my arguments kappa, s.pre, pix.pre, etc. are not what NIMBLE is expecting based on how I wrote the distribution. All of the arguments should just be one value, expect s.pre which is 2 values (an x and a y coordinate). I originally tried specifying kappa, pix.pre, omega, east, and north as double(0), but NIMBLE didn't like that either. 

Any pointers would be appreciated!
-Heather
